claim: NOT clean. First klt drc run on the committed layout/slice_routed.gds and layout/lane_column.gds, and the first at the pinned klt (.github/klt-version = 0.9.1). The five earlier records in this directory measured streams that are no longer committed; no committed record carried either input hash before this one. Layout results against a predictive PDK, not measurements. Not T1 item 3 evidence; the manifest does not cite it and item 3 stays unmet. Nothing waived, filtered or relaxed: the packaged ASAP7 deck and the full 267-id rule-category expectation set are unmodified, no --rules, no --waivers. Both runs completed; the summary-only envelopes are committed alongside this record.

klayout.engine_version_source: klayout -v on the standalone binary the deck ran under (--engine klayout shells out; --min-klayout-version 0.30.12 probed and passed)
klayout.note: The envelopes' provenance.klayout_version says 0.30.13 and sets klayout_version_mismatch: true, but 0.30.13 is the klayout Python wheel inside the pinned uvx environment, not the engine. The standalone binary that ran the deck is /usr/bin/klayout 0.30.12 -- the same version the five earlier records used. Verified by re-running the slice with --klayout-binary /usr/bin/klayout explicitly: the field still reported 0.30.13 and the violation counts were byte-identical (906, same rule_counts), so the reported version does not track the engine. Filed generically as 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#5660. There is therefore no engine-version difference between this run and the 8,208 baseline.

deck.note: Differs from the sha256:48ac590a... deck every earlier record used: the deck changed between klt 0.8.0 and 0.9.1. See the confound note below.

tool.expectation_file: 267 ids from klayout_tools.decks.asap7_rules.RULE_IDS at klt 0.9.1, sorted, one per line, unfiltered; no waivers. sha256:816302d52ed5028ee40b14ca8f41af817a32d2af747bf30c1fa2b558e89d4664
tool.expectation_file_note: Regenerated at the pin, not reused: the earlier records' 263-id file is built from the same source at klt 0.8.0, and --expect-rule-categories-file fails the run on any missing or unexpected name, so the old list cannot satisfy a 0.9.1 run. RULE_IDS was cross-checked against the deck script independently: all 123 non-interpolated .output("NAME") categories in asap7.drc are members of RULE_IDS, and the only two literal categories absent from it (FIN.GRID.1, GATE.GRID.1) are gated behind the opt-in $fin_y_origin_nm / $gate_x_origin_nm deck globals, which this run does not set. The remaining ids are the parameterized metal/via families the deck emits by string interpolation. Both runs report expectation_satisfied with empty missing_names and unexpected_names.
tool.command: uvx --from klayout-tools==0.9.1 klt drc <input> --engine klayout --deck-file <klayout_tools>/decks/asap7.drc --expect-rule-categories-file <267 ids> --min-klayout-version 0.30.12 --format json --timeout-s <1500 slice | 3600 column> --max-violations 0 -o <envelope>

envelopes_committed.why: The five earlier records could not commit their envelopes (175 MB and 3.9 GB with every polygon inline), so none of them is tool-checkable at all. --max-violations 0 makes the summary-only envelope ~30 KB, so these two are committed and are the first evidence in this directory that a tool can verify. What re-verifies portably is the input half: provenance.input.content_hash, because the GDS it names is committed in-repo and the envelope records it as a portable {path, scope: repo} locator. The deck half does not re-verify off the authoring host -- see verified.observed_off_host and caveat -- so this is a checkable input assertion, not a checkable whole envelope.

observed_authoring_host.host: the host that produced these envelopes
observed_authoring_host.scope: This is the authoring host's result only. It depends on the deck still being present at the absolute uv-cache path recorded in the envelope, which is why it does not reproduce elsewhere.

observed_off_host.host: a second host of the same fleet, same pin, 2026-11-14
observed_off_host.result: status: drifted for both envelopes (exit 3): [OK] provenance.input.content_hash, [DRIFTED] provenance.deck.content_hash with actual: None
observed_off_host.cause: --check resolves the deck by dereferencing the absolute path in the envelope's top-level `deck` field. That path does not exist on the second host, so the deck cannot be hashed and the assertion reports actual: None -- a non-resolving locator, not a content mismatch.
observed_off_host.same_bytes_is_not_enough: The second host's pinned env resolves asap7.drc to a different cache path whose sha256 is byte-identical to the recorded 14f146f0..., and --check still reports None. Passing that deck explicitly with --deck-file alongside --check is accepted without error and changes nothing (still None, exit 3).

envelopes_committed.caveat: Each envelope's top-level `deck` field is the absolute path of the deck inside the authoring host's uv cache (/home/ubuntu/.cache/uv/archive-v0/<hash>/lib/python3.13/...), because klt records the caller's resolved path. --check resolves the deck via that recorded absolute path, so the deck assertion re-verifies ONLY where that exact path exists -- not merely wherever the pinned env resolves the same deck bytes. Same env plus byte-identical deck is not sufficient, and the recorded path embeds the env's Python minor version (python3.13, where the same pin now resolves python3.14), so it is unlikely to survive a cache rebuild even on the authoring host. The input half (provenance.input.content_hash) is unaffected and re-verifies anywhere, because the envelope records the input as a portable {path, scope: repo} locator and the GDS is committed in-repo. Filed generically as 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#5709 (the host-path deck locator and the silently ineffective --deck-file override under --check); 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2723 is the closed background gap on absolute paths in reports. The envelopes are committed as the tool emitted them, unedited.

unchecked_rules.description: the ASAP7 DRM (asap7_drm_201207a.pdf (ASAP7 DRM, PDK Release 1p7; lambdapdk v0.2.17)) has no rule for the PAD layer itself (no width, spacing, area, enclosure-by-V9 or density); the deck reads PAD (stream 96/0, DRM mask 96) only as the layer enclosing V9 (V9.PAD.EN.2, V9.AUX.1), so shapes on PAD are not checked

relation.note: The same exact-16x relation the r2 pass found (16 x 513 = 8,208) still holds, so every violation in the column is on a slice instance and none is created by the column assembly.

comparison_to_baseline.confound: Two inputs changed between the 8,208 baseline and this run, not one: the deck (sha256:48ac590a... at klt 0.8.0 -> sha256:14f146f0... at 0.9.1) and the stream (sha256:2a70c692... -> sha256:4937a7bd..., re-routed from the re-synthesized netlist in #115 and reassembled in #118). The baseline stream is not committed, so the two cannot be separated by re-running, and no movement in the table above is attributed to either cause. The engine version is NOT a third variable: both runs used standalone KLayout 0.30.12 (see tool.klayout.note).

filed_tool_gaps.note: Applicability by family. This run does not re-derive the r2 pass's cell-level attribution: under --engine klayout every marker comes back with source_cell: null, so a native-deck run cannot say which cell contains a violation without mutating the layout and re-running (filed generically as 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#5661). The family identities below are inherited from the r2/components attribution, not re-measured here.

2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4496.detail: A deck-side gap, and the deck did change, so this run exercises the fix directly. The family did not clear: it is the largest single family at 9,504 (66% of the total), up from 5,824. Closed upstream, still present here.

2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4495.detail: Still open upstream, and the M1.S.* family is still present at 4,992 total (34%). It is a place-and-route fix, so nothing in this issue could have moved it.

2AMLogic/klayout-tools#4501.detail: Both families are now zero (was 64 + 48). This is the only family that cleared. Cause is not attributable from this run: it is a place-and-route fix, and the committed stream was re-routed after the baseline, so either the newer router or the deck change could account for it. The confound above applies.
